heading: CHAPTER XXII.
title: CONCERNING THE SECRETARIES OF PRINCES
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 22 treats appointments as a diagnostic. The first opinion one forms of a prince comes from the men around him, so good servants reveal princely judgment rather than merely private taste.
The chapter's middle turn matters: a prince need not be the first class of intellect if he can still recognize good and bad in another, praise the one, correct the other, and prevent deception.
The closing counsel makes loyalty structural rather than sentimental. A prince keeps a capable servant honest through honour, riches, shared cares, and managed dependence.
